answer: A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. Histories are stored in cipher, checked in summit, and nectar publishes each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 14 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm of 2227 identities would post 1618 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
